threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think 'the bus' means the double-decker. Wait till you try the old banger routes in spots that barely have a stop.
Overheard a couple arguing on the 45, she claimed he never lets her pick the takeaway. He said he only ordered what she wanted last week. Classic Brixton bustle.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a child casually say 'Wagenburg' as if it was the local playground, I knew I was really part of the Neukölln vibe.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the BVG announcements sound more like a DJ set? It's an art form, especially when they mix in those delay effects during the strikes.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: A local will complain about the 14 Mission being late, while a newcomer just waits without questioning it. The eye-roll says it all.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a free ride last New Year’s Eve. Watching a guy juggle while the bus crawled through the rain felt perfectly San Francisco.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the nightlife; they miss the quiet mornings where locals cherish their café con leche and a good book at La Pepita.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to sit anywhere but the busy terraces, fully embracing the sun while ignoring the chill of the evening.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the bus instead of checking the Overground app every five minutes. That’s classic newbie behaviour.
Last night on the 59, a guy serenaded the bus with Nirvana. By the time we hit Clapham, the whole front half was singing along. Just another night in Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid selling handmade bracelets outside the shop, while a group of old ladies discussed politics over coffee at the next table.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a bar that serves cocktails inspired by the city's exotic street art—each drink tells a visual story.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell who's local by how casually they dodge the random dog on the tracks at Civic Center. Tourists just stop and stare.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy feeding the pigeons next to a broken Muni bus at Civic Center today. Classic SF moment—chaos and calm, all in one frame.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists often think the street performers on Carrer Gran are just for fun, but many of them really rely on tips to scrape by. It’s a tough gig.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell they're recent when they order a coffee and ask for milk on the side, not realizing a cortado is the local way.
